title: How do we multiply Roman numerals?
description: Four pairs of Roman numerals are multiplied by finding the value of each answer and then building it from the biggest symbol downwards. The video shows that no simple symbol rule works. Keeko's doubt is that the two symbols can be written side by side.
teaching_notes: One idea: Roman symbols give no rule for multiplying, so we use the values and then rebuild the answer from the biggest symbol. This is why Roman numerals make multiplication hard. Watch for students who write two symbols next to each other.

source: Find V × L, L × D, V × D and VII × IX in Roman numerals.
video_script.why: The child sees that multiplying Roman numerals has no simple symbol rule, so each answer is found by value and rebuilt from the biggest symbol.
video_script.substitution: Read the value of each numeral, multiply the values, then write the answer as a sum of Roman landmark values, biggest first.
video_script.anchor: four pairs of Roman numerals to multiply: V and L, L and D, V and D, VII and IX
video_script.wrong_answer: multiply by writing the two symbols side by side
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko multiplies V and L by writing the symbols side by side. Side by side, Roman symbols only add or take away, so the row does not give 5 × 50.
video_script.payoff_line: Find the value, then build the answer from the biggest symbol

final_answer.value: V × L is CCL, L × D is 25 M's, V × D is MMD and VII × IX is LXIII
final_answer.spoken: vee times el is see see el, el times dee is twenty five em, vee times dee is em em dee, and vee eye eye times eye ex is el ex eye eye eye

hold_back: V × L is CCL, L × D is 25 M's, V × D is MMD and VII × IX is LXIII
never_show: the answer card before the last beat of the board solution
maths_rules: L × D = 50 × 500 = 25000 = 25 thousands, written as M repeated 25 times
none of the four answers is a single symbol, so there is no simple rule
video_script.design: One idea: no symbol rule gives a Roman product, so we use values. The four pairs stay on the stage and each is worked in turn.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; four pairs of Roman numerals appear: V and L, L and D, V and D, VII and IX; a question mark appears

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.pairs: the first three pairs, V and L, L and D, V and D, appear
marks.last: the fourth pair, VII and IX, appears and a question mark appears above all four pairs

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about multiplying Roman numerals.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>Multiply vee by el, el by dee, and vee by dee.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Then multiply the Roman numerals for seven and nine. How can we write each answer in Roman numerals?

beats.on_screen: the four pairs hold still and the question mark glows

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board and the question mark glows

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the pairs move to the stage; each numeral is joined to its value: V 5, L 50, D 500, VII 7, IX 9

marks.vals: V, L and D are joined to 5, 50 and 500
marks.sev: VII is joined to 7, and IX is joined to 9 with a note that it is 1 less than 10

narration: <bookmark mark='vals'/>Vee is five, el is fifty, and dee is five hundred.
<bookmark mark='sev'/>Vee eye eye is seven, and eye ex is nine, which is one less than ten.

beats.on_screen: Given: V and L; L and D; V and D; VII and IX

marks.given: the facts are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four pairs of Roman numerals, shown on the board.

beats.on_screen: To find: each multiplication, written in Roman numerals

marks.find: the words To find are written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find each answer in Roman numerals.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: V × L = 5 × 50 = 250 = 100 + 100 + 50, written as CCL

marks.m2: 250 splits into 100 + 100 + 50, and the symbols C, C, L are written under the parts

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, vee times el.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Five times fifty is two hundred fifty.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>That is one hundred plus one hundred plus fifty, written see see el.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: L × D = 50 × 500 = 25000, which is 25 thousands, written as M repeated 25 times

marks.m4: 25000 is shown as 25 blocks of 1000, with an M under each block

narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, el times dee.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Fifty times five hundred is twenty five thousand.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>That is twenty five thousands, so em is written twenty five times.

marks.m6: 2500 splits into 1000 + 1000 + 500, and the symbols M, M, D are written under the parts

narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, vee times dee.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>Five times five hundred is two thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='m6'/>That is one thousand plus one thousand plus five hundred, written em em dee.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: VII × IX = 7 × 9 = 63 = 50 + 10 + 1 + 1 + 1, written as LXIII; none of the four answers is a single symbol, so there is no simple rule

marks.m8: 63 splits into 50 + 10 + 1 + 1 + 1, and the symbols L, X, I, I, I are written under the parts
marks.m9: the four answers line up side by side, and none of them is a single symbol

narration: <bookmark mark='s4'/>Step four, vee eye eye times eye ex.
<bookmark mark='m7'/>Seven times nine is sixty three.
<bookmark mark='m8'/>That is fifty plus ten plus one plus one plus one, written el ex eye eye eye.
<bookmark mark='m9'/>None of the four answers is a single symbol, so there is no simple rule for multiplying.

beats.on_screen: Answer: V × L is CCL, L × D is 25 M's, V × D is MMD and VII × IX is LXIII
narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Find the value, then build the answer from the biggest symbol.
<bookmark mark='res1'/>Vee times el is see see el. El times dee is twenty five em.
<bookmark mark='res2'/>Vee times dee is em em dee. Vee eye eye times eye ex is el ex eye eye eye.

beats.on_screen: Keeko appears beside the board with a raised hand
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows V and L side by side; the take-away rule lights up and VL reads 45; the bubble is struck through

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows V and L side by side
marks.rule: the take-away rule lights up: a smaller symbol before a bigger one, and V L reads 45
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and 5 × 50 = 250 is shown next to 45

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we can multiply by writing the two symbols side by side, vee then el.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>A smaller symbol before a bigger one means take the smaller away. Vee el would mean forty five.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But five times fifty is two hundred fifty, so side by side cannot be multiplying.
